newsitem.title: UK: Traders unruffled by Nigeria Bonny force majeure.
newsitem.headline: Traders unruffled by Nigeria Bonny force majeure.

text.p: Traders and equity holders of Nigerian crudes showed little concern on Tuesday following Shell Nigeria's force majeure on exports of Bonny crude oil because of a strike by contractors at the tanker terminal.

"We were informed by Shell that all offshore loading activities of Bonny were suspended due to an industrial strike ....but this kind of thing in Nigerian production is normal, very normal," one regular Bonny lifter said.
Shell said on Tuesday it had declared force majeure on the 450-475,000 barrels per day Bonny loadings with effect from Monday and this would continue as long as the strike lasted.
"But usually it leads to around two days loading delays -- not much to be concerned about," another lifter said.
One trader said that storage levels at the Bonny terminal were quite low but was unsure of how many day's capacity were available.
"I don't think there is much real concern about this. (strike). It really is a normal thing for Nigeria," he said, though he did add that Shell declaring force majeure was unusual.
